description.narrative: In May 2025, the Celestial Cacao project was launched together with AsoAnei, a cooperative in the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, Colombia. The project brings together 200 farming families working to transform 375 hectares of degraded land into thriving cacao agroforestry systems.A baseline study conducted during the first phase of the project found that 51% of participating cacao farmers currently earn a living income. As climate change increasingly threatens coffee production, many families are transitioning from coffee to cacao.The project supports the two groups within the cooperative. Coffee farmers transitioning to cacao receive planting materials, tools and training to establish productive cacao farms. Cacao farmers with low yields or quality receive targeted support to improve productivity and bean quality. Experienced cacao farmers within the cooperative provide guidance and share their knowledge with other participating farmers.Inclusion is a key element of the project. Young people and members of indigenous communities receive additional opportunities to develop their careers in the cacao sector and are prioritised in project activities. Women are also prioritised through economic activities and training aimed at strengthening their participation in decision-making and increasing their involvement in cacao cultivation at cooperative, community and household level.The project also addresses the working conditions of approximately 200 workers on participating farms. Attention is given to safe and fair employment, including appropriate contracts, protective equipment and training.Celestial Cacao aims to increase the number of farming families earning a living income, while contributing to the restoration of degraded and deforested areas. Cacao offers an opportunity to address two challenges at once: improving farmers’ livelihoods and restoring nature.The project contributes to a fairer and more sustainable cacao value chain—from bean to bar.
